title: Canada international Alphonso Davies’ injury ‘doesn’t look so bad’ – Vincent Kompany
content:
Canada international Alphonso Davies suffered a fresh injury during Bayern Munich’s 3-2 win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday, but manager Vincent Kompany is hopeful that “it doesn’t look so bad”.

Davies, 25, was involved in an innocuous challenge for the ball in the 48th-minute at Allianz Arena, after which he left the field limping heavily and in obvious emotional distress, having been consoled by his teammates. He was able to walk back to the dressing room and did not leave the pitch on a stretcher.

Kompany told DAZN that: “It doesn’t look so bad. I don’t know if it’s two or four weeks. But there’s the feeling it won’t take that long.”

Bayern’s vice captain Joshua Kimmich said in the mixed zone: “On the pitch, he (Davies) was very down and sad because he quickly realized that there was an injury.

“I don’t know exactly what he has. He was a little more composed in the dressing room. We hope it won’t be too long downtime.”

The left-back tore the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee while on international duty in March of last year. Bayern Munich chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen accused Canada Soccer of being “grossly negligent” in its handling of Davies’ injury.

Davies made his first appearance in nine months after coming on in Bayern Munich’s Champions League game against Sporting CP in December. The victory over Eintracht was Davies’ 12th game back and fifth start since his return at the end of last year.

Davies was replaced by Hiroki Ito for the remainder of the game and Bayern held onto their lead, extending their gap at the top of the Bundesliga to nine points, with second-placed Borussia Dortmund due to play later on Saturday. The German side also have Josip Stanisic and Raphael Guerreiro who can deputise in that position.

“It looked like it might be something longer-term, said Max Eberl, Bayern’s board member for sport. “It has to be something muscular. He’s already being examined.”

Bayern will travel to face Dortmund next weekend at the Westfalenstadion, in a game which could decide the destination of the league title.

Analysis from The Athletic’s Canadian soccer writer Joshua Kloke

Davies has struggled with injuries throughout his career.

The ACL tear in March, while with the Canadian national team, caused him to miss most of 2025. Previously, Davies has sustained multiple muscle injuries as well as a bout with myocarditis that impacted his 2022 World Cup qualifying campaign.

The concern is therefore that another muscle injury could make being at his best for the World Cup difficult.

When Davies has been fit, his form has bounced up and down since his all-world highs of 2023, when he was arguably the best left back in the world.

Davies’ game is built on speed on the flank. Any muscle injury could hurt how well he continues to perform both for Bayern and Canada.

If Davies is in strong form, he remains arguably Canada’s best player. His pace and crossing ability can fit well — offensively speaking — into Canada manager Jesse Marsch’s high-tempo system.

But because of injury, Davies has not yet made a consistent impact for Marsch as hoped. Davies wanted to move into an advanced midfield role for the World Cup. That opportunity could have led to a possible breakout tournament for Davies under Marsch. However, his latest injury leaves that possibility in doubt.

If it gets to a point that Davies is unable even to start or compete in the World Cup, Canada should be well covered: Richie Laryea was Canada’s best player in 2025 and should be a more than adequate left back. Ali Ahmed or Liam Millar are both in contention for a starting left midfield role. Both have fans in Marsch.
